source.section: Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 350,000.00 + wages (person 1) 150,000.00 = 500,000.00. Federal taxable income = 500,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 468,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 500,000.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 500,000.00. Line 5 0.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 0.00. Line 9 base income = 500,000.00 - 0.00 = 500,000.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 500,000.00 is not greater than 500,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 5,700.00. Line 10b 0.00. Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 5,700.00. Line 11 net income = 500,000.00 - 5,700.00 = 494,300.00. Line 12 tax = 494,300.00 x 4.95% = 24,467.8500. The form takes whole dollars only and would show 24,468.00; expected uses the formula to the cent. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 24,467.85. The printed word is 'greater than', so federal AGI of exactly 500,000.00 keeps the allowance.
